title: Germany's Gen Z protests disrupted by violence on Saturday
summary: Nationwide protests led by young people were largely peaceful throughout the day, but reports about looting and rioting in the evening, especially in Frankfurt, overshadowed the spirit of the…

image.caption: Police blamed masked looters for instigating violence in FrankfurtImage: Andreas Arnold/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Clashes break out in Cologne, five detained

blocks.caption: Police officers were pelted with bottles and bicycles outside the cathedralImage: Thomas Banneyer/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Clashes broke out in Cologne on Saturday, with about 200 people involved in disturbances near Cologne Cathedral.
Police officers were attacked on the square outside the famous cathedral, with bottles and bicycles hurled toward police. One person was injured, police said.
In a nearby side street, a window was smashed by an electric scooter thrown during the unrest, police added.

blocks.caption: A smashed window at an art gallery in central CologneImage: Christoph Reichwein/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: According to regional broadcaster WDR, other groups besides Gen Z demonstrators were involved in riots.
Cologne's police chief Johannes Hermanns said it was deeply saddening that peaceful protests were overshadowed by "extremists who had nothing but violence in mind."
While Gen Z protests across Germany were largely peaceful during the day, clashes were reported in several cities as night fell.
